d: What Ghost Messaging is, and where to start.
x: Ghost Messaging is one app for the people you talk to: your texts, your friends on Ghost, your circles with their chats, calls and files, and your Telegram, Signal and other chats, side by side. Messages between Ghost apps are sealed end to end, there are no ads, and the app is open source. Ghost Messaging is in alpha It works well enough to use every day, but things still change quickly and some features are marked Coming soon . If you're testing it, start with Join the alpha , and tell us anything odd in the Alpha testers circle. Start here Install the app Android, Mac or Windows, and what to say yes to. The first time you open it The welcome, and whether Ghost takes over your texts. Your account Create one, keep your recovery words safe, sign in elsewhere. Circles A group with its own spaces: chat, voice, files and texts. Plugins Record calls, live captions, watch together, and more. Your texts on a computer Pair the Mac or Windows app with your phone. Finding your way around Everything starts from the dock at the foot of the screen. From left to right: New (start a conversation, a circle or a space, or join one), Messages , Contacts , Archive and Settings . Messages Messages Codes Circles MC Maya Chen See you at 7! 4:12 2 D Dad 📷 Picture Yesterday BC Book Club Sam: Chapter 9 tonight? Mon The conversations list, with its tabs at the top and the dock at the foot. At the top of Messages are three tabs: Messages (texts and chats), Codes (sign-in codes, kept out of the way) and Circles . A few words we use Word What it means Circle A group of people with a sidebar of spaces, a bit like a small server. You can be in as many as you like. Space A room in a circle (or on its own): chat and voice, text only, files, or an SMS space for people without the app. Friend Someone you talk to over Ghost rather than by text: added by their username, or by their number once you've sealed your texts together. Connections Your other chat accounts linked into Ghost: Telegram, Signal, WhatsApp, Matrix. Routes How messages travel between Ghost apps: over the relay, or by text. Plugin An extra you add from Settings › Plugins : for yourself, or for everyone in a circle. On which devices Android phone : everything, including your texts (SMS and picture messages). Mac and Windows : friends, circles, calls, files and your other chats on their own, and your texts when paired with your Android phone. iPhone Coming soon : friends, circles and calls. Apple doesn't let apps send or read texts outside the EU, so no texts.

Your texts aren't part of it; they stay in your phone's own store. Create an account Go to Settings › Me › Account and tap Create an account . Write down your 12 recovery words Ghost shows 12 words. Write them down, on paper, in this order, and keep them somewhere safe. Make sure nobody can see your screen. Never type them into a website or tell them to anyone. d: Recovery words, your password, the account address, and being the same you on every device.
x: You don't need any of this to use Ghost Messaging. It's here for when you want to know what your account is, where it's kept, and what happens when you sign in somewhere else. One identity, on every device Your account is a key that's yours alone, made from your 12 recovery words. Every device you sign in on becomes that same you: your friends see one person, a circle sees one member, and everything sent to you reaches each of your devices. Your username (like @alex ) is how friends find you. It points at your key. Your password unlocks a sealed backup of your key, so you can sign in with a username and password instead of the words. Your 12 recovery words are the key. They work without the password, and nothing else can replace them. The account address The address that starts with 0x , shown when your account is made and in Settings › Me › Account , is your account's public name. It's the same in any wallet app that takes your 12 words, because it's made from them in the same standard way. Ghost doesn't use it for money; it's simply the one name your account has everywhere. Sharing it is safe; sharing your words is not. What the server keeps The relay server at gogho.st keeps your username and a backup of your key, sealed with your password, which is stretched on your device first. The server can't open it. It never sees your recovery words, your password, or your messages. Kept by the server Never sent to it Your username, and the key it points to Your recovery words Your sealed backup (only your password opens it) Your password Your verified number, if you verify one, to text you codes What you write, to anyone A computer paired with your phone A Mac or PC paired with your phone used to be someone of its own. Now it can be the same you: in Settings › Me › Account on the computer, tap Become the same you as your phone , or sign in to the account your phone is in. Account Become the same you as your phone Keeps who you are now, the same you as your phone Sign in to your Ghost account The account your phone is in On a paired computer. If you lose a device Sign in on another device, with your username and password or your words. In Settings › Me › Account › Signed in on these devices , remove the lost one. It's signed out the next time it connects. If you think someone has your words, make a new account and tell your friends; the words can't be changed.

d: A space that people without the app are in by text.
x: An SMS space is a circle's chat that people without the app can be in, by text. One member's Android phone does the texting: it texts each message to everyone in it by text, and brings their replies back into the space. How it works Every message written in the space is texted from the texter's phone to each person in it by text, as Name: words . A picture or file is said in words, like (a file: menu.pdf) . What they text back comes into the space marked 📱, so everyone in the app sees it. Each person is texted on their own, so nobody's number goes to the others. The texts are sent from the texter's number and count on their phone plan. Family texts Mum 📱 Mum: Dinner at 6? Yes, I'll bring dessert In the app. Alex Alex: Yes, I'll bring dessert Dinner at 6? On Mum's phone, in her usual texting app. Make one New space › SMS space In the circle, tap New space and choose SMS space . Your phone becomes its texter. New space SMS space People without the app are in it by text, sent from your phone and your number. The texter's phone It must be an Android phone with Ghost as its texting app, and Ghost must be running for texts to go and come. Only that phone knows the numbers of the people in it. Add people by text Open the space, tap People by text in its header, and under Add someone by text enter a name and number, then Add and text them . They get a text saying how it works and how to leave. People by text Add someone by text Mum +1 555 010 0142 Add and text them Members with a verified number are in it by themselves Members of the circle who have verified their number don't need adding: when their app comes into the space, it gives the texter's phone their number, sealed so only that phone can read it, and they're texted from then on. They aren't texted their own messages. People by text marks them a member, by their linked number . Leaving Anyone in it by text can text STOP to leave. They're told, and stay out. The texter can take someone out: in People by text , tap them, then Take out of the space . They stay out too, until added again by hand.

d: What is sealed, what the server sees, blocking, and signing out.
x: Ghost Messaging is built so the people running its server can't read what you say. There are no ads, and the app is open source, so anyone can check. What's sealed end to end What Sealed end to end? Messages between friends, and in groups of friends Yes Circles and spaces: chat, files, polls Yes, with a key the circle's members share Calls Yes, directly between the people in them Your texts with one person, with encryption on Yes Ordinary texts and picture messages No: they go through your carrier, as all texts do Telegram, Signal, WhatsApp and Matrix chats As those networks seal them; they go between your device and the network, not through Ghost What the server sees Which installs talk to each other, and when, as any server passing messages would. Your username, and your account backup sealed with your password (which it never sees). Your verified number, if you verify one, to text you codes. It's shown to nobody unless you choose. Never: what you write, your files, your recovery words or your password. On your device Spam filtering, sorting, translation, summaries, captions and transcripts all happen on your device. Your texts stay in your phone's own store. Plugins say on their pages what they can see. Blocking and archiving Block someone from a conversation's menu or their card. Settings › Blocked lists everyone you've blocked, Telegram and Signal people too, and unblocks them. Archive a conversation by swiping it left. Settings › Archived (or the dock's Archive) has them; a new message brings one back. In circles A circle's messages are sealed with a key everyone in it has. Removing someone stops their app joining, but doesn't change that key: for anything a removed person mustn't read, make a new circle. See Removing someone . Leaving Settings › Me › Remove everything about me unlinks every account and your number, and clears your watch list, on the phone and on the server. Settings › Me › Account › Sign out of this device signs the device out; remove other devices from Signed in on these devices .

d: How messages travel between Ghost apps: the relay, texts, and testing them.
x: Between Ghost apps (friends, groups, encrypted texts), messages can travel more than one way. Settings › Routes shows the ways your phone reaches others, tried from the top: one that fails or gets no answer gives way to the next. Routes Routes Relay server Through a server on the internet. The server sees who talks to whom, never what is said. SMS As data texts over the phone network. Each counts as a text on your plan. The ways this phone reaches another, tried from the top. People you can reach MC Maya Chen Last by the relay server Press one to send a test and see which route carries it. Settings › Routes on the phone. The relay server Ghost's relay server (at gogho.st) passes sealed packets between apps: friends, circles, spaces and calls' setup. It can't read them; it sees only which installs are talking, as any server would. It's also where your username, your sealed account backup and a circle's sealed files are kept. SMS as a route When the relay can't be reached, a message to a friend can go as a data text over the phone network instead: still sealed, needing no internet, and reaching a phone whose app is closed. Each one counts as a text on your plan, so only small messages go this way. Test a route Under People you can reach , press someone and choose Send a test , By the relay server only , or By SMS only (one text on your plan) . Lately shows how recent messages went. Invite someone by text Invite someone by text opens a new chat with an invitation written. Choose who, change the words if you like, and send it as any text. Once they have the app and you text each other, it offers to turn encryption on between you.

d: Control the app from a script or another program, through its API.
x: Ghost Messaging has an API: every part of the app, from your conversations to its screens, as methods you can call from a script or another program. It's off until you turn it on, and only someone with your token or connection string can use it. Turn it on Developer mode On your phone: Settings › Developer , switch on Developer mode . A new section appears: Settings › API . Choose how to reach it API On this phone Serve the API Over HTTP, with a token Allow from Wi-Fi Served on the phone's address on your network too Copy the token From anywhere Through the relay Copy the connection string Serve the API : over HTTP on the phone. From a computer by USB: adb forward tcp:8765 tcp:8765 , then call http://localhost:8765 . Allow from Wi-Fi serves it on your network too. Through the relay : from anywhere. The connection string ( ghostapi1:… ) holds the key every call is sealed with; the relay passes calls along without being able to read them. Keep it as you would a password. Call a method Over HTTP, POST /api/ method with the parameters as a JSON body and your token: curl -s http://localhost:8765/api/conversations.list \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer token ' \ -d '{"limit": 5}' Or with the command-line client in the app's repository ( tool/ghost-api.mjs ): node tool/ghost-api.mjs --token token app.info node tool/ghost-api.mjs --remote ghostapi1: secret networks.chats '{"network": "telegram"}' With no method it lists them all; --doc method shows one's documentation. The methods Settings › API › Methods documents each one, with what it takes and answers and a place to try it. Those marked ⚠ change or remove something, and ask before running there.
